title: INT8/FP8 kernel handshake and async prefetch strategy to reduce dequant overhead
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem statement: The runtime currently pays a nontrivial wall-time and memory tax when switching between INT8 and FP8 execution paths during prefill/decoded streaming. This ticket implements a lightweight "kernel handshake" protocol plus an async prefetching strategy to reduce repeated dequant/requant overhead and avoid stalls at attention boundaries.

Scope: Implement kernel-level coordination between prefill and decode stages so the executor can preserve precision-compatible buffers and schedule contiguous microbatches onto a chosen precision lane. Add an async prefetcher that warms dequant buffers and kernel kernels (JIT/compiled artifacts) ahead of path switches. Deliver changes in the serving runtime, provide telemetry, and validate across small and large models (7B-70B).
background:
Recent incidents and benchmarks show 6-12% latency spikes on tail requests when the system transitions between mixed-precision kernels mid-prefill (especially when KV caches are touched). Existing mitigations (coarse-grained lane pinning and cold-start caching) reduce worst-case but increase overall cost. We need a targeted handshake that: 1) avoids full-body dequant cycles when decode remains on same logical precision for next N tokens; 2) allows cheap async materialization of dequant buffers; 3) signals kernel readiness to the scheduler to avoid last-moment kernel jit compilation stalls.

Related tickets: ENG-66321 (quant-scheduler-latency-smoother), ENG-21458 (layerwise-cast-latency-credit-bridge).
goal: Reduce median and p95 latency for mixed-precision prefill+decode scenarios by >= 8% and remove >90% of end-of-prefill stalls caused by on-path dequantization. Maintain or improve token throughput and keep cost delta <= 2% compared to baseline optimized int8-only runs.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime supports a kernel handshake API between kernel selector and executor that exposes: desired precision lane, warmup hint (microbatch count), and buffer-retention policy.
Async prefetcher implemented: can pre-allocate and pre-populate dequant shadow buffers without blocking decode path.
Benchmarks: end-to-end p50 and p95 latency measured on standard perf harness (7B/13B/70B) show >=8% improvement on mixed-precision traces compared to current mainline.
No regression on int8-only or fp8-only steady-state throughput (<1% difference).
Observability: new telemetry (handshake events, prefetch hits/misses, buffer retention counts) is visible in console and exported to perf dashboards.
Documentation: runtime API doc and brief design note added to Confluence; SDK changes (if any) documented in changelog.
Code reviews: all changes merged behind feature flag and can be toggled per-deployment tier.
Safety: feature flag default-off for private customers; opt-in test plan executed with dedicated capacity before rollout.

Emit event: prefetch.{hit,miss} with buffer_size and mem_region
Add Prometheus counters: handshake_requests_total, handshake_time_ms_bucket, prefetch_hits_total
Expose dashboard panels: handshake success rate, prefetch hit rate, p50/p95 latency for handshaked vs non-handshaked traces
benchmarks: Baseline: mainline runtime w/ old coarse lane-pinning on mixed-precision traces
Target: runtime-1.21 feature branch with handshake+async-prefetch enabled
Benchmark harness: cloud perf cluster, stable GPU fleet (A100/H100), synthetic mixed-precision traces captured from production proxy (anonymized).
Success metrics captured per-model: tokens/sec, p50/p95 end-to-end latency, memory delta, and cost-per-token estimate
risks: Increased memory pressure from retaining dequant buffers across requests; mitigated by buffer-retention policy and LRU-based eviction.
Complexity in scheduler interactions may introduce deadlocks if handshake not timeboxed; mitigate with timeout and automatic fallback.
JIT/kernel warm-up may differ across hardware; must include per-arch warmup heuristics and fallback to compile-on-demand.
Telemetry overhead if events are high-volume; sample events when QPS is high.
notes: Initial microbenchmark: small 13B model test showed 9.5% p95 reduction and 3% throughput improvement when handshake kept lane for at least 4 microbatches.
Observed a pathological case where repeated tiny requests holding buffers caused memory churn; added retention cap suggestion in design.
Coordination: needs follow-up with infra (autoscaler) to ensure warmup tasks do not trigger unbounded scaling.
